Operator Precedence Parsing
• Operator precedence grammar is a kind of shift-reduce parsing method that can be applied to a
small class of operator grammars.
• It is mainly useful for parsing arithmetic and logical expressions, where operators have different
precedence and associativity.
• An operator grammar has two important characteristics:
1. There are no € productions.
2. No production would have two adjacent non-terminals.
• The operator grammar to accept expressions is given below.
• E →E+E / E
• E →E-E / E
• E →E*E / E
• E →E/E / E
• E →E^E / E
• E →-E / E
• E →(E) / E
• E →id

• Two main Challenges in the operator precedence parsing are:
• Identifying the correct handle to reduce during each reduction step.
• Selecting the correct production for that handle so that the complete input is eventually reduced to the 
start symbol.
• To solve these challenges, the parser establishes precedence relationships between terminals
•
There are three kinds of precedence relations that will exist between the pair of terminals “a” and “b” as 
follows:
•
If a has higher precedence over b; 
a .> b
•
If a has lower precedence over b; 
a <. b
•
If a and b have equal precedence, 
a =. b
Note:
• id has higher precedence than any other symbol
• $ has the lowest precedence.
• If two operators have equal precedence, then we check the Associativity of that 
particular operator.
2
Usually indicates that the parser should SHIFT.
Usually indicates that the parser should REDUCE.

The input string: id1 + id2 * id3
After inserting precedence relations becomes: $ <· id1 ·> + <· id2 ·> * <· id3 ·> $
Basic Principle: Having precedence relations allows identifying handles as follows. 
1. Scan the string from left until seeing ·> and put a pointer. 
2. Scan backwards the string from right to left until seeing <·
3. Everything between the two relations <· and ·> forms the handle
4. Replace the handle with the head of the production.

Operator Precedence Parsing Algorithm
• Initialize: Set ip to point to the first symbol of the input string w$
• Repeat: Let b be the top stack symbol, a the input symbol pointed to by ip
if (a is $ and b is $) 
 
return 
else 
      if a ·> b or a =· b then 
               push a onto the stack 
               advance ip to the next input symbol
else 
      if a <· b then

                   c  pop the stack 
                until (c .> stack-top)
      else error

• A pedestrian suddenly crosses the road.

The importance of trustworthy machine learning (TML) is an AI-
based autonomous vehicle.

What happens if ML is NOT trustworthy?
• Consider this scenario:
• The ML model was trained mostly using daytime images. At night, it fails to recognize a pedestrian wearing dark 
clothes.
• The system predicts: Pedestrian → 
 Not detected → 
 No emergency braking → 
 Accident
• The model may have 95% accuracy in testing, but that number alone does not make it 
trustworthy.
• The key message: “High Accuracy ≠ Trustworthy AI”
• A trustworthy ML system must be accurate, robust, explainable, secure, fair, privacy-preserving, 
and reliable under real-world conditions.
